learner_operation: Read which count is supplied; rank equals pivot count, or total columns minus non-pivot count. Select the unique matching integer from five radio choices.

fixed_features.feature: Rank target, five radio options, one correct
fixed_features.justification: Every source-bank question has this response contract.

fixed_features.feature: Easy gives pivots; moderate gives non-pivots
fixed_features.justification: Observed difficulty split: direct definition versus one subtraction.
Source-like workload and rank <= min(rows,columns); feasibility does not require rank to differ from rows or non-pivots.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Pivot count or columns-minus-nonpivots, including equality with rows or non-pivots.
answer_roles.observed: Easy ranks 1..12 covered; moderate full-row-rank and rank=nonpivot cases are rejected by every profile.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Names and feasible rows preserve the response; moderate columns affect it.
answer_roles.observed: Successful controls follow these dependencies; source q-79409 rows 5 -> 4 instead fails generation.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Preserve complete banks on replay; replace colliding distractors on extensions.
answer_roles.observed: Fresh positions/orders vary in all profiles, but valid() requires the original unsigned recipe to be distinct before constructing the bank.

coverage.result: All complete banks replay. Twenty fresh seeds per profile; delivery accepts 100/100 easy and 112/120 moderate, skipping eight duplicates.
FAIL: 4x7 with three non-pivots rejected by every moderate profile.
FAIL: 3x4/two non-pivots rejected. Six even-column pairs and one additional (columns,count)=(3,2) are absent within current numeric bounds.
All five survive; ranks 10,1,11,3,8 and correct positions 5,5,1,3,2. No tested fixed action solves all five.

counterfactuals.change: Change supplied pivot/nonpivot count at fixed dimensions; additionally change moderate columns 8 -> 9.
counterfactuals.expected: Easy 5 -> 4; moderate 5 -> 6 under count 3 -> 2 or columns 8 -> 9.
counterfactuals.observed: Prompts, keys, solutions, actual native acceptance/rejection and rendered answers follow the expected changes after delivery normalization.

counterfactuals.change: Rename Q to T and change feasible rows 10 -> 11, preserving columns and count.
counterfactuals.expected: Easy and moderate rank both remain five.
counterfactuals.observed: Normalized controls preserve rank; native grading and rendered prompts/solutions agree, with updated names and dimensions.
counterfactuals.justification: Rows only bound rank once the column count evidence is supplied.

counterfactuals.change: Source q-79409 rows 5 -> 4, retaining seven columns and three non-pivots.
counterfactuals.expected: Rank remains four and the feasible item is generated.
counterfactuals.observed: Every profile rejects the after parameters. No after prompt, explanation or grader instance is available; before record was source-replayed and native-graded.
counterfactuals.justification: Rank four is feasible with four or five rows; canonical example uses four.

stages_examined: task sampling without replacement; no invalid-item resampling
actual publisher normalization and inventory/within-batch deduplication
native selector inspection and faithful conditional replay
delivery.result: Rejected constructions cannot enter delivery. All five exact batch records survive. Selection depends on difficulty/freshness; conditional replay documents specified weights/history and synthetic future IDs.

limitations: Captured inventory basis 5404; later inventory changes are not predicted.
Active learner history/weights and future entity IDs are absent; selection scenarios are explicitly conditional.
Finite shortcut probes do not establish universal absence. Some numerical-order heuristics outperform chance in small groups but have counterexamples.
Historical stored q-79405 ordering weakness reproduced in affected-inventory.json is not attributed to current v2.
Canonical example has no bank; its failure concerns the valid stem, without requiring an invented canonical bank.
